questions.explanation: Involving the team in the decision-making process increases engagement and ensures better implementation of changes.

options: Accept the gift this once but tell them not to do it again.
Thank the client but politely decline, explaining that company policy prohibits accepting gifts.
Accept the gift and share it with the whole team so no one person benefits.
Accept the gift but do not tell your manager about it.
questions.explanation: Upholding company policy while remaining polite ensures consistency and prevents potential conflicts of interest.
questions.question: A client offers you an expensive bottle of wine as a 'thank you' for your help, but your company has a strict 'no gifts' policy. What do you do?

options: Stop talking to the colleague and only communicate via formal emails.
Wait for your annual performance review to mention the personality clash.
Invite the colleague for a coffee to discuss how you can work together more effectively.
Ask your manager to move your desk to the other side of the office.
questions.explanation: Direct communication is the most efficient way to resolve internal disagreements and maintain a positive culture.
questions.question: You have a personality clash with a colleague, which is starting to affect the team's productivity. How should you proceed?

options: Suggested a trial period for both ideas to see which one performs better.
Insist that your idea is better because you have more experience in the field.
Give in to the colleague's idea to avoid an argument, even if you think it is wrong.
Ask the rest of the team to vote on which idea they prefer.
questions.explanation: Compromise and evidence-based discussion are key to resolving professional disagreements.
questions.question: You and a colleague have different ideas on how to approach a new project. How do you resolve this?
You accidentally overhear a private conversation between directors about potential redundancies. What should you do with this information?
options: Tell your friend, but make them promise not to tell anyone else.
Post a vague status on social media about 'big changes coming soon'.
Discuss the information with your family to get their advice on your job security.
Keep the information confidential and do not discuss it with anyone.
questions.explanation: Confidentiality is a legal requirement; sensitive information must only be shared with authorised personnel.

questions.question: You are assigned a task that you have never done before and are unsure where to start. What is the best approach?
options: Start the task immediately and hope you figure it out as you go.
Review the task requirements and schedule a brief meeting with your manager to clarify the objectives.
Wait until the deadline is closer to see if someone else offers to help.
Delegate the task to someone else who might know more about it.
questions.explanation: Planning and seeking clarification early prevents errors and demonstrates a proactive work ethic.

questions.question: You arrive at your retail job to find a colleague hasn't turned up, leaving you alone during a busy period. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Prioritising immediate customer safety and service while notifying colleagues is the best way to manage unexpected shortages.
options: Close the shop immediately until the other staff member arrives.
Call the staff member and shout at them for being late.
Contact your manager to inform them of the situation and continue to serve customers as best you can.
Ignore the customers and focus on doing the morning admin tasks.

questions.question: You have been invited to an internal interview for a promotion. How should you prepare?
options: Research the company thoroughly and prepare examples of your previous successes.
Wing it on the day to ensure your answers sound natural and unscripted.
Focus only on your technical skills and ignore any questions about teamwork or culture.
Tell the interviewer what you think they want to hear, even if it isn't entirely true.
questions.explanation: Preparation and active listening show respect for the interviewer and help you provide the most relevant answers.
Punctuality is a sign of professionalism. Even small delays should be communicated to avoid inconveniencing others.
options: Run into the meeting 10 minutes late and apologise profusely without an explanation.
Send a quick message to the meeting organiser as soon as you know you will be late, giving your estimated arrival time.
Skip the meeting entirely because you are already late and will miss the start.
Blame the public transport system for the delay, even if you just left the house late.
questions.question: You are running 10 minutes late for a team meeting due to an unexpected train delay. What is the most professional action?

questions.explanation: Encouraging contribution from everyone ensures diverse perspectives and prevents individuals from dominating.
options: Tell the quiet members they must speak up or leave the meeting.
Ignore the quiet members and focus on the ideas being presented by the more vocal ones.
End the meeting early since not everyone is participating.
Ask specific questions to the quieter members to encourage them to share their views.
questions.question: During a brainstorming session, two team members are dominating the conversation while others remain silent. How do you handle this?

questions.explanation: Peer support helps maintain team standards and gives the colleague a chance to improve before formal action is taken.
options: Report them to HR for a breach of the dress code policy.
Make jokes about their clothing in front of the team to embarrass them into changing.
Privately and kindly mention the dress code policy to them in case they were unaware.
Ignore it, as what they wear does not affect their ability to do the job.
questions.question: A colleague has started wearing very casual clothes that go against the company's formal dress code. How do you respond?
You have promised a report to a stakeholder by 5 PM, but it is now 4 PM and you still have two hours of work left. What is the best course of action?
questions.explanation: Acknowledge errors and manage expectations regarding deadlines to maintain trust with stakeholders.
options: Contact the stakeholder as soon as possible to explain the delay and provide a new deadline.
Submit a rushed, low-quality version of the report on time.
Avoid the stakeholder's calls until you have finished the report.
Ask a colleague to give the stakeholder the bad news for you.

questions.explanation: Understanding why a process exists can help identify if it is still necessary or if there is a more efficient way to achieve the same result.
options: Stop following the process and do it your own way instead.
Complain to your colleagues about how much time the process wastes.
Ask your manager why the process is in place and suggest a more efficient alternative with evidence.
Do the process as slowly as possible to show how inefficient it is.
questions.question: You find a particular administrative process to be very time-consuming and inefficient. What should you do?
You are assigned to a high-priority project with someone you personally dislike. How do you handle the situation?
options: Request to be taken off the project because you cannot work with that person.
Focus on the project goals and maintain a professional, polite relationship with the person.
Tell the client that your colleague is difficult to work with.
Only communicate with the person when absolutely necessary and keep it brief.
questions.explanation: Professionalism involves separating personal feelings from work responsibilities to ensure the best outcome for the client.

questions.question: You see a colleague who doesn't work in the finance department taking sensitive files from the finance office late at night. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Protecting the company's reputation and security is a priority. Reporting suspicious activity is a professional duty.
options: Assume they have permission and do nothing.
Wait and see if they mention it to you later in the day.
Report your observation to your manager or the security team immediately.
Confront the person and demand to see what they were taking.

questions.question: A colleague sitting next to you frequently takes personal calls on speakerphone, which is distracting you. What is the most effective approach?
options: Speak to the colleague privately and explain how their distractions are impacting your work.
Buy a pair of noise-cancelling headphones and say nothing.
Email the whole team asking everyone to be quieter in the office.
Move your desk to a different room without telling anyone.
questions.explanation: Direct, private communication allows the colleague to address their behaviour without public embarrassment.

questions.question: The company's website has crashed, and customers are unable to place orders. How should you communicate this to inquiring customers?
options: Tell them the system is working fine and it must be their computer.
Explain that there is a technical issue, apologise for the inconvenience, and give an estimate of when it will be fixed.
Ignore the emails from customers until the system is back up and running.
Blame the IT department and give the customers the IT manager's direct phone number.
questions.explanation: Honesty and providing a realistic timeline for resolution are the best ways to handle technical failures.
